# Research report 1 of 2

I found nothing dated on or before 2026-08-30 showing that any proof of the Navier-Stokes problem had been announced, much less broadly accepted by mathematicians. Most of my searches returned September and October 2026 coverage, which is past the cutoff, so I left it out.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no URL or data series behind this question. It resolves on the market creator's judgment of whether "mathematicians widely agree the proof is probably valid" by 2027-06-03. That rule comes from the creator's clarification of 2026-06-05. [Manifold market](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/will-navierstokes-be-considered-sol)
- The Manifold page refused my connection, so I couldn't confirm the creation date, the comments or the price history directly.
- The closest official reference is the Clay Mathematics Institute's list of open problems. In the pre-cutoff material I found, the problem was still unsolved. Poincaré remains the only Millennium Prize Problem that has been solved. [Wikipedia: Millennium Prize Problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-08-30)
- Nothing before the cutoff settles the question. I found no public proof claim from before 2026-08-30 that experts were seriously reviewing.
- 2026-02-01: A Manifold market on David Budden's claimed Lean proof of Navier-Stokes resolved to "No proof / doesn't compile" at 99%. His claim failed. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Simon74fe/outcome-of-david-buddens-navierstok)

## 3. Recent news (newest first, through 2026-08-30)
- 2026-08-26: A Brown University feature on Javier Gómez-Serrano's lab said its AI approach had found singularities in related equations. This raised hopes for Navier-Stokes, but the work was described as ongoing. I only saw this through a search summary because the page wouldn't load. [Brown](https://www.brown.edu/news/2026-08-26/javier-gomez-serrano-lab)
- August 2026: Anthropic said an experimental Claude improved a long-standing bound related to the Riemann hypothesis. This is a sign of fast AI progress in math, but it has nothing to do with Navier-Stokes. [explainx summary](https://explainx.ai/blog/claude-navier-stokes-millennium-prize-rumor-fact-check-2026)
- 2025: Researchers including Google DeepMind teams reported numerically discovered unstable singularities in fluid equations. None had been rigorously proved. [Physics World](https://physicsworld.com/a/neural-networks-discover-unstable-singularities-in-fluid-systems/)
- 2024-07-09: Córdoba, Martínez-Zoroa and Zheng proved finite-time blowup for a forced, weaker-dissipation (hypodissipative) version of Navier-Stokes. This is a step toward blowup constructions but not the Clay problem. [arXiv 2407.06776](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06776v1)
- 2024-10: Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa posted a blowup result with a smooth forcing term for a related model equation (the porous-medium "IPM" equation). [arXiv 2410.22920](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22920)
- Scope caveat: forced-equation blowup results may not count as solving the Clay problem in the way people commonly understand it. How the creator would treat such a result is unclear.

## 4. Base rates
- 2000 to 2026: one of seven Millennium Problems was solved in about 26 years (Poincaré). Navier-Stokes went unsolved for its whole 26 years before the cutoff. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)
- Perelman posted his proof in 2002-2003, and broad expert consensus came around 2006. Even a correct proof took about three years to be accepted.
- Mistaken proof claims are common, for example Otelbaev in 2014 and Budden in January 2026. Very few survive expert review.
- A rough base rate for "solved and broadly accepted within a given 12 months" is low, a few percent at most. The new factor is AI-assisted proofs checked in Lean, a formal proof-verification language, which could shorten the time verification takes.

## 5. Other forecasts
- This market: search snapshots showed roughly 16-19%, but I couldn't confirm the dates of those snapshots. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/will-navierstokes-be-considered-sol)
- Related Manifold markets (snapshot dates also unconfirmed):
  - "Solved by 2030": about 26-32%. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Supermaxman/will-the-navierstokes-equations-be)
  - "When will it be solved": median around 2035. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/strutheo/when-will-the-navierstokes-problem)
  - "Will Anthropic announce a claimed solution before end of 2026": about 28-34%. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/JimMcMillan/will-anthropic-announce-a-claimed-s)
  - "Serrano and DeepMind publish a Navier-Stokes result by 2027": price not found. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/AffineTyped/serrano-and-google-deepmind-publish)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Possible AI-assisted proof announcements from Google DeepMind with Gómez-Serrano, Anthropic or OpenAI. AI labs were clearly competing on major math problems going into late 2026.
- 2026-09-11: Gómez-Serrano was scheduled to give a Harvard CMSA lecture, "Millennium Prize Problems Lecture: Navier-Stokes existence or breakdown." [Harvard](https://www.math.harvard.edu/event/millennium-prize-problems-lecture-javier-gomez-serrano-navier-stokes-existence-or-breakdown/)
- Signals to watch if a claim appears:
  - Lean formalization.
  - Public statements from leading analysts such as Tao and Fefferman.
  - Any statement from Clay.
  - Whether the result covers the forced or the unforced case.
  - Any priority disputes over who did the work first.
- Resolution depends on the creator's reading of "wide agreement," so expert commentary in the months before 2027-06-03 will matter most.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I could not find anything dated on or before 2026-08-30 showing that Navier-Stokes is solved or that a serious full proof had been claimed. Most of what the searches returned was published after the cutoff, so I excluded it.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL is given. The market's own rule says it resolves YES only if mathematicians "widely agree the proof is probably valid" by 2027-06-03, which means expert consensus decides it, not one official database. The nearest official signal is whether the Clay Mathematics Institute lists the problem as solved.
- I could not open the Manifold market page ("Will Navier-Stokes be considered solved on June 3th 2027?", by user Bayesian): the proxy refused the connection. Its creation date, the comments, and its price on or before 2026-08-30 are unconfirmed. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/will-navierstokes-be-considered-sol)
- There is a date inconsistency in the question. It says "a year from now (market creation date)" with a 2027-06-03 deadline, which implies creation around 2026-06-03. I found no news from around that date that would explain why the market was created.

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-08-30)
- 2000 to 2026-08: the Clay Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem is officially unsolved. Its official statement allows four outcomes: proofs of smoothness (A, B) or counterexamples showing blowup (C, D), where C and D allow an external force. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navier%E2%80%93Stokes_existence_and_smoothness)
- I found no pre-cutoff source showing a proof that mathematicians accept, or even a widely discussed claimed proof. Nothing settles or nearly settles the question in either direction.

## 3. Recent news (pre-cutoff, newest first)
- 2025-11: Physics World reported that Google DeepMind and university collaborators used physics-informed neural networks to find unstable singularities in fluid equations, including bounded 3D Euler. This is progress toward computer-assisted blowup proofs, not a Navier-Stokes proof. [Physics World](https://physicsworld.com/a/neural-networks-discover-unstable-singularities-in-fluid-systems/)
- Undated: secondhand Chinese and Korean coverage (HyperAI) says Demis Hassabis predicted a Millennium Prize problem would fall within a year or so, and describes a DeepMind "Operation Navier-Stokes" team of about 20. This is unverified, with no primary source. [hyper.ai](https://hyper.ai/en/news/44427)
- 2024-10: Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa proved finite-time blowup with a smooth-in-space force for the IPM fluid model (arXiv 2410.22920). This is groundwork for forced-blowup approaches. [NYU/Buckmaster notes](https://cims.nyu.edu/~tristanb/ipm.pdf)
- 2024-07: Córdoba, Martínez-Zoroa and Zheng proved finite-time singularities, with finite energy and a forcing term, for fractional Navier-Stokes with weak dissipation. That is a related model, not the Clay problem. [arXiv 2407.06776](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06776v1)

## 4. Base rates
- 2000 to 2026: one of the seven Millennium problems has been solved, Poincaré. Perelman posted the proof in 2002 and 2003, and Clay recognized it in 2010, so expert acceptance took roughly 3 to 4 years and formal recognition about 7. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Prize_Problems)
- 2014: Mukhtarbay Otelbaev's claimed Navier-Stokes proof was found flawed within weeks. Claimed proofs of this problem have historically failed. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navier%E2%80%93Stokes_existence_and_smoothness)
- Implication: the chance of reaching broad consensus within about 9 to 12 months has historically been very low. It would mostly depend on a credible claim appearing, ideally with machine-checked (for example Lean) verification, which could shorten review time.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not get a pre-cutoff price for this Manifold market. Related Manifold markets exist, including "Will Anthropic announce a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium problem before IPO?" and "Will Anthropic announce a claimed solution to Navier-Stokes before the end of 2026?", but I found no prices for them dated on or before 2026-08-30. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/did-claude-just-solve-navier-stokes), [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/JimMcMillan/will-anthropic-announce-a-claimed-s)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market, and no expert survey, on this exact question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any announcement from AI labs (DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic) or academic groups working on forced-blowup constructions. A blowup with an external force is a recognized route under alternatives C and D, and active groups include Córdoba/Martínez-Zoroa, Buckmaster and coauthors, and Gómez-Serrano with DeepMind.
- Statements from the Clay Mathematics Institute, and reactions from leading analysts such as Tao, Buckmaster and Gómez-Serrano, to any claim.
- Whether any claim comes with a full formal (Lean) verification, which would bear directly on "widely agree probably valid."
- Not found: any scheduled event before 2026-08-30 that is known to deliver a resolution.

Evidence for No:
- No credible claim existed at the cutoff.
- Budden's claimed Lean proof failed in February 2026, and Otelbaev's 2014 claim failed within weeks.
- Most claims fail.
- Even a valid claim might not win wide agreement within months, especially a forced-case or computer-assisted proof whose scope is debated.

(e) No scenario: AI labs publish further numerical and partial blowup results, maybe even a claimed proof in late 2026. Experts remain cautious through mid-2027, or the claim covers only a model equation, so the creator resolves No.

Yes scenario: DeepMind and Gómez-Serrano publish a computer-assisted, Lean-formalized forced-blowup proof for 3D Navier-Stokes in late 2026. Tao and other leading analysts publicly endorse it within months, and the creator resolves Yes.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 2%. I move up substantially, to around 8-10%, because:
- AI capability in math is visibly accelerating.
- Credible teams are explicitly targeting this problem, and the forced-blowup route is concrete.
- Formal verification could shorten the consensus timeline.
- Related markets and the hint of a later claim point the same way.

I stay below the Manifold price of about 17%. That market is thin, its snapshots are undated, it is likely inflated by hype, and wide acceptance within nine months is a high bar.

Probability: 9%

- Forced-blowup groundwork exists (Córdoba, Martínez-Zoroa and Zheng in 2024).
- Rigorous computer-assisted or Lean-verified proofs from credible experts could be accepted much faster than Perelman's was.

Yes scenario: In late 2026, DeepMind, Gómez-Serrano and coauthors post a computer-assisted proof of forced or unforced blowup with rigorous interval arithmetic. Tao and other analysts publicly say it looks right by spring 2027.
